description:
Our team is dedicated to exploring the growing challenge of discarded and abandoned equipment on the Moon and Mars. As space exploration expands, landers, rovers, instruments, protective materials, and other hardware may remain behind after missions end.

We aim to study this issue from both an environmental and technological perspective, investigating how discarded equipment can affect future exploration, scientific research, and the preservation of extraterrestrial environments. Our team explores innovative approaches for tracking, managing, reusing, recovering, or safely handling space equipment.

Through teamwork, research, creativity, and engineering, we hope to contribute ideas that support responsible and sustainable exploration of the Moon and Mars.
summary: INFINITE VOID – The Hardware We Left Behind is an educational storytelling website exploring human made equipment left on the Moon and Mars after space missions. Our six member team researched official NASA and European Space Agency (ESA) resources to understand the history, purpose, scientific contributions and mission outcomes of selected landers, rovers and scientific instruments. We developed a digital platform that presents these findings through engaging stories and visual experiences, helping visitors discover what happened to the technology after each mission ended. By highlighting the difference between intentionally retained equipment and inactive or separated mission hardware, our project brings attention to an often-overlooked part of space exploration. It addresses the challenge by making this information accessible and connecting historical missions with the future of lunar and Martian exploration. We hope to encourage scientific curiosity and greater awareness of the legacy and responsibilities of exploring other worlds.
details:
🌍 Details

INFINITE VOID is an educational storytelling website exploring the human made equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars after space missions. Through historical research and storytelling, we highlight the purpose of different spacecraft, landers, rovers and scientific instruments, their mission achievements, and what happened to them after their missions ended.

Our six member team researched information using official NASA and European Space Agency (ESA) websites and other space related resources. We developed the project to connect the history of space exploration with future missions, encouraging awareness of scientific discoveries, technological development and responsible exploration beyond Earth.

💻 Tech Stack

  • Website development: https://www.figma.com/community/file/1703809894816985359
  • Core Architecture & Languages: Semantic HTML5, Modern Vanilla JavaScript (ES6+ Modules, modular object-oriented classes with zero heavy framework bloat for maximum 60 FPS performance), and Advanced CSS3 (CSS Grid, Flexbox, custom design tokens, backdrop filters, and responsive clamping).
  • 3D Graphics & WebGL Engines:
    • Three.js (r186): Powers the interactive 3D Physics Lanyard Cards in the Team section with real-time rope/cloth physics, multi-layer canvas textures, double-sided materials, and pointer drag interactions.
    • OGL (High-Performance Minimal WebGL): Powers the 3D Infinite Spherical Menu in Cosmic Discoveries, mapping 144 dynamic tiles onto an interactive revolving sphere with custom shaders, momentum inertia, and smooth tile activation.
    • GSAP (GreenSock Animation Platform): Drives smooth staggered menu transitions and card state animations.
    • IntersectionObserver API: Hardware-accelerated viewport tracking for 1-page snap scrolling and dynamic floating navigation state without CPU-heavy polling loops.
  • Design System: Pure matte dark luxury aesthetic (#000000, #09090b, #18181b, #27272a) with custom typographic hierarchy (Space Grotesk, Orbitron, Rajdhani, Instrument Serif).
  • Website hosting: Vercel https://infinitevoid-tau.vercel.app/
  • Deployment Architecture: Zero-configuration Jamstack static edge deployment connected directly to Git.
  • Global Edge Network (CDN): Instant asset delivery worldwide with sub-50ms Time to First Byte (TTFB).
  • Performance & Reliability: Automatic HTTP/2, Brotli compression for heavy 3D assets/textures, instant cache invalidation, atomic zero-downtime rollouts, and built-in TLS 1.3 / SSL encryption.
  • Interactive website sections and visual experiences
  • Cinematic Hero Experience (#hero-page): Video-masked kinetic typography, ambient audio controller, and interactive explore launcher.
  • 25 NASA Historic Relic Missions (#missions-page): Interactive continuous option wheel selector, live telemetry status displays, and full dossier integration (mission-detail.html).
  • 3D Infinite Spherical Cosmic Discoveries (#infinite-menu-page): WebGL-powered 3D sphere with 13 celestial bodies, drag-to-spin inertia, tile recentering, and a ⌘K command-palette search dropdown.
  • Why This Mission Matters (#why-us): Interactive Earth systems and space preservation narrative detailing planetary material recovery and orbital debris mitigation.
  • Fullscreen Deep Space Story Experience (#frame-screen): 4-phase media scrubber featuring synced video transitions, sound toggle, and keyboard hotkeys (Esc, M).
  • NASA Scientists & Pioneers Showcase (#scientists-section): Editorial profile experience featuring an interactive diagonal ribbon carousel.
  • Inside NASA Cleanroom Facilities (#inside-nasa-section): Interactive facility inspector detailing mission preparation environments.
  • Scientific Reference Folders (#research-section): Interactive 8-category digital folder system with animated tabs and direct citation links to peer-reviewed NASA papers.
  • Interactive 3D Team Lanyard Stage (#team-section): Draggable Three.js ID cards with real-time physics, double-sided credential rendering, social links, and an animated parallax starfield.
  • Matte Floating Up/Down Navigation: Sleek, minimalist floating chevrons that automatically hide on Hero and Team sections and enable smooth full-screen section jumping.
  • Responsive web design : 
  • Confirmed: Yes, fully responsive across all device classes.
  • Fluid Clamp Typography & Dimensions: Built using CSS clamp(), min(), vw, and vh units, ensuring seamless scaling from 320px mobile screens up to 4K ultra-wide desktop monitors.
  • Unified Touch & Gesture Physics: 3D WebGL sphere and Three.js physics lanyards utilize Pointer Events (pointerdown, pointermove, pointerup), offering identical touch-drag, flick, and rotate fluidity on iOS/Android as on desktop mice.
    • Mission Option Wheel automatically shifts from a dual-pane desktop split to an ergonomic mobile layout.
    • Command-palette search adapts to viewport widths (min(180px, 50vw)) with mobile-optimized tap targets.
    • Floating navigation dock dynamically resizes for smaller touch displays.

Innovation Highlights

  • 🚀 Historical Storytelling: Explores the stories behind human made hardware left on   the Moon and Mars.
  • 🔬 Scientific Research: Presents mission information and discoveries using recognised space-science sources.
  • 🌍 Educational Value: Makes space exploration history accessible to students, educators and space enthusiasts.
  • 🪐 Interactive Experience: Combines educational content with visual and interactive website sections.
  • 🔭 Future Exploration: Connects previous mission experiences with the challenges and possibilities of future Moon and Mars exploration.
